title: Webb County Moves Ahead on Up to $400,000 for Veterans Treatment Program
excerpt: Webb County commissioners approved applying for a Texas Veterans Commission grant of up to $400,000 that could expand the county's veterans treatment program to as many as 30 participants, according to KGNS.
content:
Webb County commissioners have approved applying for a Texas Veterans Commission grant worth up to $400,000 to expand the county’s veterans treatment program, according to KGNS.

If the county wins the award, the program could grow to serve as many as 30 participants, offering case management and counseling alongside help with rent, mortgage payments and utility bills.

The help would not stop at the Webb County line. The program would reach into seven other counties, including Dimmit, Jim Hogg and Zapata, KGNS reported.

The grant requires no matching money from the county.

Commissioners took up the item at their Monday meeting, where the court also considered air-to-water machines for colonias and a new tracking system for the Medical Examiner’s Office — items Webb Watch 956 covered when the agenda was posted.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 26, 2026.
